record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Which families of dynamical systems are universal in the sense discussed in the paper?

evidence.quote: Question 5.5 (Rodriguez Hertz). Which families of systems are universal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of Borel dynamics. A Borel dynamical system is a pair (X,T) where X is a standard Borel space and T:X→X is a Borel automorphism. For an invariant Borel probability measure μ on (X,T), let h_μ(T) denote the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. A Borel system (Y,S) is said to embed into (X,T) on a μ-full set if there is a Borel injection π:Y'→X, defined on a T-invariant Borel set Y'⊆Y with μ(Y')=1, that conjugates S|_{Y'} to T|_{π(Y')}.

Following Hochman, call a free Borel system (X,T) universal if for every free Borel system (Y,S) and every S-invariant ergodic Borel probability measure μ on Y with h_μ(S) strictly less than the Borel entropy h(X,T) := sup{h_ν(T) : ν an ergodic T-invariant Borel probability measure on X}, the system (Y,S) embeds into (X,T) on a μ-full set. More generally, for t∈(0,∞], call (X,T) t-universal if it is free, carries no ergodic invariant measure of entropy ≥t, and contains an s-universal subsystem for every s<t.

Problem. Characterize, as broadly as possible, the families of Borel (respectively topological or smooth) dynamical systems that are universal in this sense. In particular, identify natural dynamical, geometric, or combinatorial properties (e.g., specification-type conditions, hyperbolicity, partial hyperbolicity, expansiveness) that imply universality, and determine which classes of systems—beyond mixing shifts of finite type, mixing sofic shifts, mixing positive-recurrent countable-state Markov chains, β-shifts, synchronized subshifts, and Axiom A diffeomorphisms restricted to their basic sets—are universal.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research program in Borel/topological dynamics initiated by Hochman (building on Krieger's generator theorem). Universality has been established for several specific classes (mixing SFTs, mixing sofic shifts, mixing positive-recurrent countable-state Markov chains, β-shifts, synchronized subshifts, Axiom A diffeomorphisms; also systems with the weak specification property, by Burguet and others). However, a complete characterization of which families are universal remains open, with ongoing research extending universality to broader classes.

status_evidence.title: Isomorphism and embedding of Borel systems on full sets
status_evidence.snippet: Mixing shifts of finite type are h(X)-universal; framework of t-universality introduced by Hochman.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes universality for mixing SFTs and related symbolic systems, leaving broader characterization open.

status_evidence.title: Topological and almost Borel universality for systems with the weak specification property
status_evidence.snippet: Universality is extended to systems satisfying weak specification.
status_evidence.claim: Active extensions of universality to new classes indicate the broader classification remains a developing program.

status_evidence.title: The work of Mike Hochman on multidimensional symbolic dynamics and Borel dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing universality results and open directions.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys universality results and notes that identifying all universal families is an ongoing line of research.
